From: Dana Whitfield
To: Gabriel Fontes, Victor Alade
Subject: Margin clarification needed before Thursday

Gabe, Victor –

Ahead of Thursday's board discussion, I need the gross margin figure for Q3 explained in plain terms. Specifically, the 41.2% we reported versus the 43.8% from Q2 – what drove the drop? I have my own numbers on COGS and pricing, but I want your read before I put this in front of the board.

Please send a short note (bullet points are fine) with the key drivers by Wednesday end of day. If you have a supporting schedule, attach it – I’ll pull what I need from that.

Thanks,
Dana

---

From: Gabriel Fontes
To: Dana Whitfield
Subject: Re: Margin clarification needed before Thursday

Hi Dana,

Here's the plain-English read on the Q3 gross margin drop from 43.8% to 41.2%:

- Product mix shift: We sold a higher proportion of lower-margin items in Q3, pulling the blended rate down.
- Freight and logistics costs were up about 1.1 points on higher fuel surcharges and expedited shipping for two customer orders.
- One-time vendor rebate credit of roughly $18K was booked in June per our accrual policy (landed after the June statements cut), which flattered Q2's margin slightly. Excluding that, the underlying drop is closer to 2.0 points.
- Pricing held steady; no broad discounting.

I'm happy to walk through the full COGS bridge if helpful before Thursday.

Best,
Gabriel Fontes

---

From: Dana Whitfield
To: Gabriel Fontes
Subject: Re: Margin clarification needed before Thursday

Gabe, Victor –

Thanks for the quick read, Gabe. That tracks with what I have on COGS, but I need one more piece before I finalize for the board. Can you confirm the dollar impact of the product mix shift versus the freight increase? I want to quantify each driver separately, not just points.

Also, if you have the COGS bridge schedule you mentioned, please attach it. I'll use that to build the board slide.

Need this by Wednesday EOD.

Dana

---

From: Gabriel Fontes
To: Dana Whitfield
Subject: Re: Margin clarification needed before Thursday

Hi Dana,

Happy to break out the dollar impact for each driver. Based on the Q3 COGS bridge:

- Product mix shift: approximately $310K of the gross margin dollar decline versus Q2.
- Freight and logistics increase: approximately $180K of the decline, driven by fuel surcharges and expedited shipping on two customer orders.
- One-time vendor rebate credit in June (~$18K): this flattered Q2's margin; excluding it, the underlying combined driver impact is roughly $472K.

Pricing was flat, so no dollar impact there.

I don't have a formal COGS bridge schedule in a separate file at the moment, but I can put together a simple one-page schedule summarizing the above with the Q2-to-Q3 numbers. Would that work? I can send it over this afternoon if so.

Best,
Gabriel Fontes

---

From: Victor Alade
To: Dana Whitfield
Subject: Re: Margin clarification needed before Thursday

Dana –

Gabriel's numbers are accurate. To lock it down for the board slide, here's the dollar impact per driver versus Q2:

- Product mix shift: ~$310K
- Freight/logistics increase: ~$180K
- June vendor rebate credit (flattered Q2): ~$18K
- Pricing: flat, no dollar impact
- Net underlying decline excluding the rebate credit: ~$472K

I'll send over a one-page COGS bridge schedule with the Q2-to-Q3 numbers by Wednesday EOD, so you can pull the detail straight into your slide.

V

Gabriel Fontes

From: Dana Whitfield
To: Victor Alade, Gabriel Fontes
Subject: COGS bridge schedule received — one last confirmation before Thursday

Victor, Gabe –

Got the one-page COGS bridge schedule, thanks. The dollar impacts per driver are exactly what I needed to build the board slide:

- Product mix shift: ~$310K
- Freight/logistics increase: ~$180K
- June vendor rebate credit (flattered Q2): ~$18K

I want to be certain we're not putting a number in front of the board that we'll have to walk back. If there's any variance—even a rounding difference—flag it now, not Thursday morning.

Also, for the slide I'm planning to show the net decline both including and excluding the June rebate credit. That way the board sees the true underlying trend without the one-time distortion. Let me know if either of you sees a problem with that framing.

Appreciate the speed on this. I'll have the final slide ready by end of day tomorrow.

Dana
